description: LifecycleRecord places one lifecycle event in a run or project log.

anyOf.description: Complete marks the durable end of a run log. RecordingError reports an earlier failure in another log owned by the run; an absent Complete means the run log itself did not finish durably.
Interrupt records a request to stop a running session.
PlannerDecision records the task selected for the next dispatch. An absent Task records that the planner ended dispatch.

task.description: Task is one assignment selected by a Loop planner.

name.description: Name is a short label for recognizing the work.

description.description: Description states the desired result and any necessary, non-obvious information. It leaves the approach to the worker.

definition_of_done.description: DefinitionOfDone says how to recognize successful completion of this assignment. It does not declare that the enclosing goal is complete.

validation.description: Validation describes evidence the workflow can gather. Either field may be empty; the workflow still assesses the task against DefinitionOfDone.

command.description: Command is a known executable check.

query.description: Query is a question for a validator agent.

anyOf.description: RunCancelled records a workflow run stopped by context cancellation.
RunEnded records the result of a workflow run.
RunStarted records the beginning of a workflow run.
ScopeBegan records entry into one scope instance.

anyOf.description: ScopeEnded records exit from one scope instance.

SessionClosed records that a scope closed one of its sessions. Error is set when the session had a native id and the adapter's Close failed; a session that never allocated a native id is always closed cleanly.
SessionCreated records a new agent session or fork.
Steer records a message sent to a running session or dropped after it ended.
SuperviseAttached records a reviewer attached to a worker turn.

interval.description: A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants as an int64 nanosecond count. The representation limits the largest representable duration to approximately 290 years.

anyOf.description: TurnEnded records the result and accounting for one agent turn. Usage is what the turn spent, per model: the harness's own turn report when it stated one, and otherwise the turn's step events summed under the session's model.

result.description: JSONText is JSON source text carried opaquely by an event. Complete events contain one encoded value; delta events may contain only the next fragment. Text preserves provider-specific payloads while the event remains a closed Polytype shape.

items.description: ModelUsage is what one model spent, under its name. The run log carries a turn's usage as one entry per model: the type grammar the log's schema is generated from has no map shape.

tokens.description: Tokens is what one model read and wrote, in the five fields every adapter reports. A field the provider does not report is zero: zero is a number, and no field is ever omitted.

input.description: Input is the uncached prompt: the provider's input tokens less the cache read (and less the cache write where the provider folds it in).

output.description: Output is the visible output: the provider's output tokens less the reasoning tokens.

reasoning.description: Reasoning is the reasoning or thinking tokens.

cache.description: Cache is the prompt tokens the cache served and the prompt tokens written into it.

read.description: Read is the prompt tokens served from cache.

write.description: Write is the prompt tokens written to cache.

duration.description: A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants as an int64 nanosecond count. The representation limits the largest representable duration to approximately 290 years.

anyOf.description: TurnStarted records the beginning of one agent turn.
ValueSet records one value written into a scope.

value.description: JSONText is JSON source text carried opaquely by an event. Complete events contain one encoded value; delta events may contain only the next fragment. Text preserves provider-specific payloads while the event remains a closed Polytype shape.
